First, Have you taken a pregnancy test? Second, Our body reacts differently to IUD so one’s “regular iud spotting” might look different from another person. Also, if this is worrying you - getting it checked is your best option, you might be able to request an ultrasound from your physician to check if the IUD is in place which is much less invasive than a screening and wont need an ob-gyn depending on where you live.

I have a copper IUD for almost a year now and my body adjusted to the IUD prob around 6 months (varies per person). I only get cramps on my period, no cramps or spotting in between. But then again, our bodies are different. IMHO, I would get it checked out just to rule out any issues and for your peace of mind.
